newsitem.title: USA: Cuban immigrant set to die in Florida for murder.
newsitem.headline: Cuban immigrant set to die in Florida for murder.

text.p: A Cuban immigrant convicted of murdering an Orlando teacher was scheduled to die on Tuesday in Florida's electric chair, despite his claims of insanity and an appeal for mercy from the Pope.

By Monday, Pedro Medina, 39, was in a holding cell at Florida State Prison near Starke, awaiting either a last-minute reprieve or the electric chair, where he was scheduled to die shortly after 7:00 a.m. EST (1200 GMT) Tuesday.

Medina was found guilty of the 1982 murder of Dorothy James, 52, a physical education teacher who was found stabbed to death. He was apprehended with the murder weapon while driving her Cadillac automobile in northern Florida.

He was first scheduled to die for James's death on Dec. 5, but the case was automatically delayed when his attorneys raised the insanity defence, saying Medina did not know what he was doing when he killed James.

Mental health experts hired by the defence testified that Medina was delusional, but experts appointed by the court said he was faking to stay alive. A panel of psychiatrists reviewed the case in mid-December and found Medina sane.

In January, Archbishop Agostino Cacciavillan, apostolic pro-nuncio for Pope John Paul II, asked Florida Governor Lawton Chiles for clemency, saying, "A gesture of mercy in this case would greatly contribute to the promotion of non-violence and of mutual respect and love in society."

Medina had ordered his last meal by Monday. A Department of Corrections spokeswoman said he had asked for steak with onion and garlic gravy, cheese, French fries, tossed salad, black beans and rice, coconut pie, butter pecan ice cream with strawberry syrup and a Pepsi soft drink.
Under Florida law, an inmate can be executed if he understands he was convicted of murder, that he was sentenced to die and that carrying out the sentence will kill him.

Since Chiles signed Medina's death warrant in November, Medina has claimed to have conversations with Albert Einstein, drank from the toilet in his cell and eaten his own feces during a court hearing.
Since the U.S. Supreme Court reinstated the death penalty in 1976, 38 prisoners have been executed in Florida.
